codes.sample: The CFPB Making Ends Meet survey, a nationally representative US adult sample drawn from credit records and fielded from January 2025 (N = 2,630, weighted). The survey had 263 past-year sports bettors, of whom 187 bet online.
codes.sports_betting_definition: Past-year sports betting: "Have you placed a bet on a sporting event or outcome in the last year?" Mobile betting was asked as a follow-up: "Did you use a mobile phone to place a bet?"
codes.pg_instruments: None. The only gambling measures were betting frequency, typical bet size and largest single-day loss, plus difficulty paying bills that respondents put down to gambling losses.
codes.possible_duplicate: None identified. The data are the 2025 Making Ends Meet public-use file, which other reports could also use.
codes.note: No problem-gambling screen. "High-intensity gambling" (33.8% of sports bettors, 93 people) means betting at least weekly, a typical bet over $50, or losing $100+ in one day. The author says it "is not necessarily a sign of problematic gambling" and suggests future studies use the PGSI. Gambling losses as a reason for difficulty paying bills is a harm item, not a screen.

codes.sample: The sample is not described. The paper reports unnamed "respondents", mostly aged 18-24, on attitudes, awareness and the influence of digital technology. No sample size, recruitment method or gambling participation is given. The methods section lists only desk sources: "Academic journals, market reports, legal documents, government publications".
codes.sports_betting_definition: Not defined for any sample. Online sports betting, fantasy sports and esports betting are mentioned only as market segments; sports betting participation is not measured.
codes.pg_instruments: None. No problem-gambling screen, diagnostic interview or ad hoc problem-gambling items are reported. Addiction is discussed only in general terms, citing the literature.
codes.note: Mainly a market and policy review of online gambling in India. Its Results summarise a small opinion survey (technology influence, legalisation, awareness, age) that is not described. No problem-gambling instrument and no figure for sports bettors. E4 chosen because people were surveyed; E5_design (review/policy paper) is a reasonable alternative.

codes.sample: 685 past-12-month bettors from the UK (n=435), Hungary (n=112) and Canada (n=138), surveyed March–July 2024. Recruited through Betway (emailed its users), a Midnite website banner, the GameStar gaming magazine/Facebook post, and a Prolific pilot (n=19). Split into esports bettors (n=359; 96.1% also bet on traditional sports) and sports-only bettors (n=326).
codes.sports_betting_definition: Bet on traditional sports and/or esports in the past 12 months. Groups: those who bet on esports in the past 12 months (most also bet on sports), and those who 'had only bet on traditional sports in the year preceding data collection'.
codes.pg_instruments: PGSI (past 12 months). The paper describes the 0, 1–2, 3–7 and 8–27 categories, but reports only mean scores.
codes.possible_duplicate: Same author group (Mangat, Demetrovics, Czakó; University of Gibraltar), with data collected via Betway and Midnite in 2024. Other publications from this esports bettor dataset may exist.
codes.note: Table 1 (p.5) gives only mean PGSI scores: 'Problem gambling symptoms 3.53 (4.42)' for esports bettors and '2.03 (3.06)' for sports bettors, plus odds ratios in Table 2. No count or % in any PGSI category is reported for either group, so none can be derived. Recruited through operators, not selected for gambling problems. No race-only bettors.

codes.sample: 186 US/English-speaking adults with probable OCD (OCI-R ≥21) recruited via Reddit OCD groups, OCD clinics and support groups; online cross-sectional survey on AI chatbot use in OCD. Not recruited for gambling problems.
codes.sports_betting_definition: Past-month esports betting (single item, Table 3); also 'esports betting is preferred method of gambling'. No other sports betting measured.
codes.pg_instruments: MIDI DSM-5 Gambling Disorder Module, self-report, past year, ≥4 of 11 criteria = gambling disorder; G-SAS given only to those with GD.
codes.possible_duplicate: Same survey ('A Pilot Study Assessing Generative AI Chatbot Use in OCD', Grant et al., Univ. of Chicago) may feed other publications on AI or internet use in OCD; none cited here.
codes.note: Table 3 p.4: past-month esports betting 57.6% (GD, N=34) vs 3.0% (no GD, N=152), by GD status only; no esports-bettor total or GD rate among bettors. Percentages don't fit the Ns (57.6% fits 19/33; 3.0% gives no whole count of 152), so back-calculation is unreliable. Esports is past month, GD past year. Consider 'unclear' if approximate derivation is accepted.

codes.sample: LENAD III is a nationally representative household survey of Brazil (2022–2023), age 14+. The analysed module is split-questionnaire version 2 (N=4,842). Past-year gamblers who completed the PGSI: N=674 (28 missing). Of these, 32.1% (weighted) used online gambling platforms ('bets').
codes.sports_betting_definition: Sports betting is not measured on its own. 'Online gambling was defined as participation in internet-based gambling platforms, including sports betting websites and virtual casino games' (past 12 months). This mixes sports betting with online casino.
codes.pg_instruments: PGSI (past 12 months). Categories: 0 no risk, 1–2 low risk, 3–7 moderate risk, 8+ problem gambling. Also 'any risk' (PGSI ≥1).

codes.possible_duplicate: This uses the same LENAD III data as Pio et al. 2026 (Braz J Psychiatry, 'The Gambling Landscape in Brazil...'; ref 35) and the UNIFESP LENAD III reports and recommendations (refs 22, 37). Spritzer 2011 and Tavares 2010 come from the earlier LENAD I wave, so they are a different sample.
codes.note: PGSI results exist only for a combined 'online gambling' group (sports betting sites plus virtual casino). There is no separate sports-betting group. Only weighted % are given. The unweighted n of online gamblers is not given, only 32.1% (weighted) of the 674 gamblers. If the reviewer accepts 'bets' as a stand-in for sports betting, reconsider, but counts can't be derived.
